patch.value: GH-1664: pm context --for orient --limit 3 and pm activity --limit 3 reparse every history stream, so a three-row recent-activity read pays archive-scale I/O

GitHub issue #1664 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4 from an agent-UX audit). On a 3,188-item tracker copy with about 124 MB of history in 3,206 streams, the reporter measured p50 16.36 s for pm context --for orient --limit 3, 6.10 s for pm context --limit 3 and 8.21 s for pm activity --limit 3 on a shared, contended host. Source confirms the algorithm: the orient context builds its activity section through runActivity with compact output and a small limit (src/sdk/query/context.ts), and collectActivityEntries in src/sdk/query/activity.ts lists every .jsonl file in the history directory and calls readHistoryEntries on each, so time filtering, sorting and the row limit apply only after the whole archive is parsed. The limit bounds delivery, not history I/O. One uncontended run on this repository's own tracker (126 MB, 3,217 history streams) on 2026-11-05 took 3.27 s for pm context --for orient --limit 3, against 1.48 s for pm context --limit 3 and 1.61 s for pm activity --limit 3, so the activity section roughly doubles the cost of the canonical cold-start read, and that cost grows with history volume rather than item count. Expected: a bounded recent-activity read uses a coherent recent-event index or revision-keyed per-stream summaries, reads only enough verified tails to fill the window and the requested rows, falls back explicitly when the index is unavailable, and keeps history policy and integrity checks, with invalidation on append, replacement, repair, redaction and compaction. Why it matters for agents: every reconnecting agent and parallel worker pays a full-history scan in the canonical cold-start read to obtain three events. Related open work on other axes: pm-801d indexes item files with zero output change, pm-29ymfn owns strict history verification cost, and pm-1wujzi owns the claim-state history fold. The same orient read is the subject of the budget defect pm-gh1662. Duplicate check: searched activity history scan, recent activity index, context latency, history volume scaling and collectActivityEntries across all statuses, and no item owns the activity read's full scan.

pm activity --limit N and the activity section of pm context read a bounded number of history entries, independent of total history volume, when a valid recent-event index or per-stream summary is present; The index or summary is derived, rebuildable and never authoritative: it is invalidated on append, replacement, repair, redaction and compaction, and a stale or missing index falls back to the full scan with an explicit receipt field naming the fallback; pm activity and pm context output is identical with and without the index on the same corpus, proven by a spec that includes redacted and compacted streams; scripts/bench gains a scale budget for a three-row pm context --for orient read on a fixture with thousands of history streams and at least 100 MB of history, with a declared p50 ceiling that CI fails on regression; Negative control: forcing the full-scan path on the benchmark fixture exceeds the declared ceiling
On a tracker with thousands of history streams, time pm context --for orient --limit 3, pm context --limit 3 and pm activity --limit 3. The orient and activity reads scale with total history volume
A three-row recent-activity read costs time proportional to the rows and window it returns, not to the size of the history archive

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Root cause, measured 2026-11-20 on this repository (3,354 streams, 135 MB): two archive-scale costs sat in the canonical cold-start read. (1) The context activity section called runActivity in compact mode, which has no lower time bound, so it parsed every stream, sorted every entry and then fingerprinted every matching row (stableStringify plus sha256, 1.6 s of a 4.96 s orient in a CPU profile) for a page cursor that context discards. (2) pm activity's default 24-hour digest parsed every stream to find the few entries inside its window. Fix: a derived runtime/history-stream-summary.json (src/core/history/stream-summary.ts) records per stream the entry count and oldest/newest canonical timestamps under its stat signature (dev, ino, size, mtimeNs, ctimeNs). An entry is trusted only while that signature is unchanged and the read that recorded it began more than two seconds after the stream's last change (Git's racy-clean rule), so every writer (append, redaction, compaction, repair, restore) invalidates it without cooperation; inode 0 and non-files never earn trust. runActivity skips trusted streams outside [from, to); context uses readRecentActivity, which reads untrusted and irregular streams first, then trusted regular streams in the activity order of their newest entry until the next one cannot outrank the last selected row (ties decided by item id). Read hooks keep the complete read (same rule as the metadata cache), and trackers under 500 streams never write the summary. Unbounded reads disclose history_read / activity_history_read with summary_missing, summary_invalid, summary_stale, read_hooks_active or unwindowed_query plus streams_read and streams_total. Results: orient 4.96 s -> 1.45 s, pm activity --limit 3 2.36 s -> 0.90 s (pm list --limit 3 is 0.85 s); pm activity in 8 modes and pm context orient produce byte-identical JSON to the released 2026.11.20 build under a fixed PM_CLOCK, receipts excluded.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Evidence and scope notes. Specs: tests/unit/core/history/stream-summary.spec.ts (12: canonical timestamps, bounds, minimum, read hooks, missing/racy/append/same-size rename/stale, 14 malformed summary shapes, unwritable runtime directory, ino 0); tests/unit/commands/history/activity-bounded-reads.spec.ts (8: ten activity queries plus readRecentActivity equal the complete read on a corpus with a real history-redact stream, a real history-compact stream, old, tied, irregular and empty streams, and stay equal after append, redaction, compaction, restore, update, history-repair --salvage-tail and a raw append that moves an old stream into the window; a stream corrupted after its bounds were trusted raises the same history_json_invalid as the complete read). Benchmark: scripts/bench/history-read-costs.mjs (in pnpm quality:static) on 2,000 streams and 216 MiB measured bounded p50 1,045 ms vs full-scan p50 2,951 ms; the declared ceiling is 1,672 ms, the bounded p50 must stay under 0.6 of the same-runner full scan on every runner, and on a qualified runner the full scan must exceed the ceiling (negative control). The first read of a fresh fixture is excluded because it builds the SQLite history event index; that cold-start cost (about 6 s of a 20 s first orient on a fresh copy of this tracker) is filed as pm-s7z78x. Also parallelized enforceHistoryStreamPolicyForItems existence probes (130 -> 90 ms on 3,000 items) and added the summary to pm gc --scope runtime.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 1 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh, working tree): seven findings, six fixed. (1) The equal-timestamp branch of streamCanOutrank had no executions: a new spec makes four streams tie at the top-N cutoff, including an untrusted stream that fills the selection first while a tied stream with a smaller id must still be read, and unit-tests both comparators. (2) A damaged summary record with a matching signature could hide a non-empty stream: parseStoredStream now accepts only bounds summarizeHistoryStreamBounds can produce (empty means no timestamps and regular, a regular non-empty stream has both timestamps, timestamps appear together and in order). (3) One trusted stream suppressed the stale receipt after a bulk rewrite: summary_stale now applies once more than half of the streams lack current bounds. (4) A zero activity limit skipped every stream, so a damaged stream no longer raised its error: the untrusted and irregular streams are read for any limit, and only trusted regular streams are skipped. (5) A fractional SDK limit was passed raw to the collector, so the cutoff never filled: readRecentActivity passes the floored limit. (6) Distinct file names that collate equally (NFC vs NFD) could swap rows at the cutoff: file position is now the final tie-breaker in selection and stream ordering. Declined with reason: (7) a stream the window reaches is still parsed in full; bounding inside a stream needs an append-verified byte boundary (an in-place rewrite of equal or larger size defeats a size check), so it is filed as pm-kyf4z2 and the docs state the actual bound (the streams with entries in the window, not the archive).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh): seven findings, all fixed. (1) A well-formed but damaged summary (a newest timestamp moved earlier) passed validation and record() never repaired it because the signature still matched: the file now carries a sha256 checksum of its streams payload and any mismatch makes it summary_invalid. (2) On a shared tracker another user could stat but not read a stream the first user's summary skips, hiding the complete read's EACCES: the reader's uid is part of every stream signature, so another reader's bounds are never trusted. (3) The newest-N loop re-sorted the whole selection after every stream, quadratic for a large --activity-limit: rows now accumulate unsorted and the pool is cut back to the limit only once it doubles; between cuts the stop check uses the last cut's row, which ranks no higher than the true cutoff, so stopping stays sound. (4) bench --update could raise the committed ceiling: it now keeps the committed ceiling unless --allow-increase <reviewed reason> is given (the regenerated ceiling ratcheted from 1,672 to 1,652 ms). (5) A tracker whose current bounds are mostly irregular pruned nothing yet emitted no receipt: a new irregular_timestamps reason covers it. (6) The negative control compared the full scan with the nominal ceiling while the bounded check adds a 100 ms margin: both now use the enforced ceiling. (7) enforceHistoryStreamPolicyForItems re-probes each missing stream before creating it, so a stream created meanwhile (by another writer or an earlier creation's write hook) is neither reported as auto-created nor passed to a write hook; tests/unit/core/history/history-stream-policy.spec.ts covers both and the chunk boundary.

value.text: Codex review round 3 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh): seven findings, all fixed. (1) A stream that vanished between the stat and the read (directory moved aside and restored) was recorded as empty under its unchanged signature: activity now reads through readHistorySnapshot and record() keeps bounds only when the byte length read equals the observed size. (2) Every Windows account shared the reader identity '-': the reader is now the OS account (uid on POSIX, account name where there is none) from os.userInfo, and no stream earns trust when neither is available. (3) The file-position map held every discarded candidate and its patch payload: it uses weak keys, and the pool is cut back during the first pass as well, so a three-row read retains rows proportional to its limit. (4) Half stale plus half irregular crossed neither threshold: stale and irregular streams count together and the larger cause names the receipt. (5) A write hook that removes a later stream after the bulk probe left it missing under auto_create: with write hooks active every id is probed sequentially right before its turn (hasActiveOnWriteHooks), as before this change. (6) The benchmark child inherited a caller's PM_CLOCK/PM_SEED, which could empty the activity window: it drops PM_CLOCK, PM_CLOCK_TICK_MS and PM_SEED. (7) The packaged report linked into .agents/pm: it uses the canonical GitHub URL labelled repository-only. Separately the absolute ceiling headroom is 2.0x (reset once through --allow-increase with a recorded reason, now 1,984 ms) because the min() ratchet followed the fastest local run; the runner-independent 0.6 fraction gate stays primary.

value.text: Codex review round 4 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh): six findings. Rounds 3 and 4 each found another way the path and the bytes can diverge (a vanished stream, then an equal-sized swap during a restore), so instead of another path check the record is now anchored on the open file: activity reads through readIdentifiedHistorySnapshot (src/core/history/read.ts), which fstats the handle that supplies the bytes, and record() stores bounds under that handle's signature and only when the bytes are the whole of that file; no path change can bind bounds to a revision that did not supply them. Also fixed: (2) the negative control could fail a faster runner whose full scan stays under the ceiling; in --check the absolute ceiling is now enforced only where it discriminates (qualified runner and full scan above the enforced ceiling) and otherwise reported unverified with a reason (runner_unqualified or full_scan_within_ceiling), while --update still refuses a ceiling its own measurement cannot prove; (3) sessions of one uid with different supplementary groups shared trust: the reader identity is uid, gid and sorted groups on POSIX; (5) a non-string recorded agent_harness crashed runActivity's provenance matcher with unknown_error (pre-existing, also in 2026.11.20), filed and fixed as pm-sew1dj so raw, recent and provenance reads all return the row; (6) the CLI spec now pins PM_PATH and PM_GLOBAL_PATH inside its fixture. Declined with reason: (4) owner-only permissions for the summary: it discloses strictly less than the item metadata cache (runtime/metadata-cache.json, titles and bodies) and the history streams themselves, which pm writes with the default umask, so restricting this one derived file would not change what a co-tenant can read; tracker-wide runtime permissions would be their own change.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 5 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh): five findings, four fixed. (2) getuid/getgid are real ids and the identity was cached for the process: the reader identity is now the effective uid, effective gid and current supplementary groups, computed once per summary session, so a long-lived SDK host that drops privileges never reuses bounds. (3) Disabled sessions (under 500 streams, read hooks active) paid an extra handle stat per stream: they read through the plain readHistorySnapshot. (4) A path-validation error in the bulk existence probe preempted an earlier sorted id's refusal or creation: such an id stays a candidate and raises at its own turn. (5) commit() could recreate a tracker removed during the read through writeFileAtomic's recursive parent creation: it now creates only runtime/ beneath an existing tracker and writes without parent creation. Declined with reason: (1) re-validating every skipped stream after the read. A complete read is not an atomic snapshot either (docs already state continuation keeps no atomic cross-file snapshot): a stream that changes while either read runs may or may not be reflected, depending on whether the change lands before that stream is reached. A second bulk stat of every skipped stream would add tens of milliseconds to every bounded read to narrow, not close, that window; docs/COMMANDS.md now says so explicitly.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 6 (gpt-6.2-sol, xhigh): four findings, two fixed. (3) pm activity --json --stream built its own meta record and dropped history_read: the meta record now carries it. (4) unwindowed_query fired whenever --from was absent, even when a --to before most of the archive pruned every stream (streams_read 0): it now applies only when the read parsed most streams, the same majority rule as the stale receipt. Declined with reason and filed as pm-4zqpr3: (1) attribute-caching network mounts and (2) Windows tokens of one account sharing trust. Both are properties of every stat-keyed derived cache, the item metadata cache first (ADR pm-vnie), so the summary copies an accepted trust model rather than introducing one; a fix belongs in one tracker-wide policy (statfs-detected network filesystems or a setting, token elevation on Windows). docs/COMMANDS.md now states that limit instead of claiming credential isolation on Windows.

A three-row recent-activity read costs time proportional to the streams its rows and window reach, with output identical to the complete read and an explicit receipt whenever it could not be bounded

Added runtime/history-stream-summary.json (src/core/history/stream-summary.ts): per-stream entry count and oldest/newest canonical timestamps keyed by the stat signature of the open file that supplied the bytes plus the reader's effective credentials, trusted only outside a two-second racy window, checksummed, never authoritative, engaged at 500 or more streams and bypassed under read hooks. runActivity skips trusted streams outside its window; pm context's activity section uses the new SDK readRecentActivity, which reads newest-first until no unread stream can outrank the cutoff. Unbounded reads disclose history_read / activity_history_read (summary_missing, summary_invalid, summary_stale, irregular_timestamps, read_hooks_active, unwindowed_query). scripts/bench/history-read-costs.mjs gates a three-row orient on 2,000 streams and 216 MiB in pnpm quality:static with a 0.6-of-full-scan fraction, a ratcheted declared ceiling and a full-scan negative control. Also parallelized stream existence probes and added the summary to pm gc --scope runtime.
Bounded recent-activity reads shipped with derived per-stream bounds, a newest-rows context path, fallback receipts and a CI-gated benchmark

value.before: ActivityResult and ContextResult had no read-cost disclosure, and the context activity section was built by a full runActivity page over every history stream
value.after: ActivityResult gains an optional history_read receipt and ContextResult an optional activity_history_read receipt ({ reason, streams_read, streams_total }), present only when a read on a tracker with 500 or more history streams could not be bounded by its window; readRecentActivity({ limit }, global), ActivityHistoryReadReceipt and RecentActivityResult are new exports of @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/query; rows, totals, cursors and errors are unchanged
value.migrate: No change for existing reads. Consumers that reject unknown result keys should allow the optional history_read and activity_history_read receipts; a consumer that needs only the newest rows can call readRecentActivity instead of runActivity with raw: true
